Q9.note: Line traces the far skyline across the full width: left Aiguilles/Jorasses serrations, the Mont Blanc flanks and dome shape, then the Chablais ridge on the right (Dent d'Oche dot sits on a summit). Largest discrepancy is a ~0.7%-width lateral offset on one right-hand peak; vertical fit is well within 1.5%, with no roll.

R2.note: Line climbs steeply from left (well below the skyline) to right (high in open sky above the Chablais ridge). Its shape does not match the Mont Blanc outline or the other ridges, and labels such as Mont Vuarat and Les Pleiades fall in haze or on plains.

T5.note: Essentially the same pose as Q9. The line follows the left serrated skyline, the Mont Blanc profile and the right-hand Chablais peaks, with only a small lateral offset on one right peak, sub-1% vertical error and no tilt.

photoNote: Telephoto view from the Jura across the Swiss plateau toward Mont Blanc and the Chablais. The distant skyline is hazy but clearly visible against the sky across the whole frame.
